WITH category_averages AS (
    SELECT
        pc.product_type_description,
        AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS average_quantity,
        AVG(ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) AS average_difference
    FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili
    JOIN Products AS p
        ON p.product_id = ili.product_id
    JOIN Product_Categories AS pc
        ON pc.production_type_code = p.production_type_code
    GROUP BY pc.product_type_description
),
category_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_difference) AS mean_average_difference
    FROM category_averages
),
above_mean AS (
    SELECT
        ca.average_quantity,
        ca.average_difference,
        ca.average_difference - cm.mean_average_difference AS excess_difference
    FROM category_averages AS ca
    CROSS JOIN category_mean AS cm
    WHERE ca.average_difference > cm.mean_average_difference
)
SELECT
    AVG(average_quantity) AS average_of_category_average_quantity,
    AVG(average_difference) AS average_of_category_average_difference,
    AVG(excess_difference) AS average_excess_over_category_mean
FROM above_mean;

assumptions.assumption: `product_quantity` is text in the schema, so it is cast to REAL for averaging; values that cannot be converted to numbers are treated according to the database engine's cast behavior. The query otherwise follows standard SQL aggregate null handling.
The mean of category averages includes each category with a non-NULL average difference once, and categories are grouped by `product_type_description`.
